findings.doc_quote: ChangeType is a union of literal value, C.* condition instance, glob string, or callable (value) -> bool .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/types/types.py:330 — "FalseySentinel | V | Condition[V | FalseySentinel] | ComparisonCondition[V | FalseySentinel] | None"; src/hassette/event_handling/predicates.py:765 — `return coerce_to_literal_type(actual, condition) == condition`. Probe: P.StateTo("o*") on a new state of "on" returns False.
findings.explanation: ChangeType has no glob member, and a string is compared by equality as a plain literal. Only P.ServiceDataWhere wraps glob strings (predicates.py:700-701), and that happens in its own __post_init__. A value such as changed_to="o*" (bus.py:1761 passes it to P.StateTo unchanged) or P.StateTo("o*") matches only the literal string "o*".
findings.suggested_fix: ChangeType is a union of literal value, C.* condition instance, or callable (value) -> bool. A plain string is compared exactly; use C.Glob for glob matching (P.ServiceDataWhere is the exception and auto-wraps glob strings).

findings.doc_quote: condition accepts a literal value, a C.* condition instance, a glob string, or any callable (value) -> bool .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/predicates.py:321-322 — `extracted = self.source(value)` / `return compare_value(extracted, self.condition)`; predicates.py:763-765 — non-callable conditions use equality, with no is_glob check. Probe on entity light.kitchen: P.ValueIs(source=A.get_entity_id, condition="light.*") returns False; condition=C.Glob("light.*") returns True.
findings.explanation: P.ValueIs does not detect globs. A glob string is treated as a string literal and compared exactly, so it silently never matches real entity IDs.
findings.suggested_fix: condition accepts a literal value, a C.* condition instance (use C.Glob for glob patterns; a bare glob string is compared literally), or any callable (value) -> bool.

findings.doc_quote: The context dict from the event payload.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/events/base.py:31-32 — `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` / `class HassContext:`; src/hassette/events/hass/hass.py:221 — `"context": HassContext(**event["context"])`. Probe: type(A.get_context(evt)) is HassContext, and isinstance(..., dict) is False.
findings.explanation: get_context returns a frozen HassContext dataclass, not a dict. Its fields are read as attributes (ctx.user_id), and it defines no __getitem__, so dict-style access such as ctx["user_id"] fails. The adjacent Returns column (HassContext) is correct; the description contradicts it. The accessor's own docstring (accessors.py:240) has the same error.
findings.suggested_fix: The HassContext dataclass from the event payload (fields: id, parent_id, user_id).

summary: The page is highly accurate: signatures, defaults, coercion rules, operator behavior and accessor return values all matched the code, most of them confirmed by executing the real predicates. There are three errors. Two are one mistake repeated: lines 9 and 28 say glob strings work as conditions, but only P.ServiceDataWhere auto-wraps them, so elsewhere they silently fail to match. The third is line 141 calling the HassContext dataclass a dict.
